name: Leucine
info: A hydrophobic BCAA. It differs from isoleucine in the position of the branch.

history.clue: The name comes from the Greek word for “white,” after the appearance of its crystals.
history.story: In 1820, Henri Braconnot isolated white crystals while breaking down muscle tissue and named the substance leucine: leukos means “white” in Greek. A year earlier, Proust had obtained the same substance while studying cheese, but gave it a different name. It was not until 1839 that the two were shown to be the same compound.
